title: Shift-work checkpoint contract v1
$comment: Encodes checkpoint contract v1 (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-10-shift-work-checkpoint-contract-draft.md) plus the two driver-forced deltas: plan.units[].role (model dispatch without reading briefs) and state.external[].until_cmd (machine-checkable wait, replacing prose `until`). Re-planning needs no schema change: a planner unit is just a unit. STRICTNESS POSTURE: `version` is const-pinned to 1 so a reader can refuse unknown majors; every object the driver or a session reads by field name sets additionalProperties:false, and every field the draft's schema block shows on every instance is required (empty arrays are legal, so a fresh checkpoint is cheap to write). The two exceptions are `history[]` and `retro[]` items: those are the free-text annotation space the draft treats as notes, so they allow extra keys (e.g. a session adding `seq` or `tokens`) while still requiring their load-bearing fields. `units[].commits` is optional because the draft only carries it on completed units. `state.external[].status` is a non-empty string rather than an enum: the draft closes the enum for unit status (the driver's SUCCESS test) but never enumerates external status, and inventing values here would reject honest checkpoints. `plan.cursor` must name an existing unit id — JSON Schema cannot express that cross-reference, so the driver checks it structurally and escalates on a dangling cursor. Serialization: checkpoints are YAML for humans per the draft, but the v1 driver reads JSON only (stdlib-only rule), so sessions driven by driver.py write .json; this schema validates the parsed document either way. AMENDMENT (job46/AS-2, docs/roadmap-agent-stack.md): `job.roles` is a THIRD v1 addition, beyond the two driver-forced deltas named above, and it is OPTIONAL — a checkpoint that omits it is exactly the document the rest of this comment describes, and every checkpoint written before it existed still validates unchanged. Both CLAUDE.md files say the model a unit runs on is `per role, never random, always logged`; logged it was, in `history[]`/`retro[]`, which are the two objects here that allow extra keys, so nothing could ever compare the model a role was ALLOWED to use against the model that answered. `job.roles` is that declaration, and it sits on `job` because that is where a reader already looks for the rules binding every unit. It is a MAP (unit role -> the model identifiers that role may report), not a record the driver reads by fixed field name, so the closure the rest of this file spells `additionalProperties: false` is spelled here as `propertyNames` over the SAME three names `plan.units[].role` enumerates, with `additionalProperties` carrying the value schema once instead of three times: a key outside the role enum is refused, and so is a value that is not a non-empty array of non-empty strings (an empty list would be a rule no session could satisfy, which is a typo and not a policy). A role the map does not name is unconstrained — declaring one role does not silently forbid the others. The ENFORCEMENT is not here: this file states the contract and the runtimes state the refusal, so no example error text appears in these descriptions. `version` stays 1 because nothing already in the document changes meaning: a reader that ignored `roles` would still read every other field correctly. What it would not do is enforce the rule — and since `job` is closed, an older reader does not ignore the key, it refuses the whole file. That refusal is the intended behaviour and not a gap: opening `job` so an old reader could skip the key is what would make this check bypassable by running an older bantamkit. AMENDMENT (job50/F8): `handoff.notes` is a FOURTH v1 addition and, like `job.roles`, OPTIONAL, so every checkpoint written before it validates unchanged. `handoff` was the one closed object with nowhere to put a fact that is not an imperative, a question, or a prohibition — a gate baseline, a last commit, a technique worth reusing — and the ledger shows sessions inventing a key for each such fact, being refused, and folding the fact into `next_action` prose instead. The field is a STRING and `handoff` stays `additionalProperties: false`: the defect was the absence of a place for a sentence, not the strictness, and a misspelled `next_action` is refused after this amendment exactly as it was before. The reason it is a string and not a map is in its own description.

version.description: Contract major version. A reader that does not know this value must refuse the file.

done_definition.description: Ground truth that ends the job — a check, not a vibe.

constraints.description: Invariants binding every unit, copied verbatim into each session.

roles.description: OPTIONAL. Per unit role, the model identifiers a session in that role may report. Omit it and the job behaves as it always has: the model is recorded and nothing compares it to anything. A role this map does not name is unconstrained; only a role named here is held to its list. Keys are the `plan.units[].role` enum, so a role that is not a role is refused rather than quietly ignored.

additionalProperties.description: The model identifiers this role may report, spelled exactly as a session logs them. Non-empty: a role allowed no model is a typo, not a policy.

authorized.description: OPTIONAL (#225). The irreversible verbs the user granted for this job (merge, tag, publish, ...), written once at plan time. Declared, clock_in escalates on a unit whose `irreversible` verb is not listed; absent keeps today's behaviour.

kind.description: OPTIONAL (#264, #265). `investigation`: the job answers `question` by testing `hypotheses` in run units, each supported claim replayed by another role before `conclusion` may say resolved. `experimentation`: candidate units compete in their own worktrees on `experiment.objective`, each validated by another role at the exact SHA it submitted. Absent = today's job.

direction.description: Which way a better score points.

base_sha.description: The commit every candidate starts from. Frozen: once a brief or clock-out has read it, a checkpoint that says otherwise is refused.

harness.description: The command that scores a candidate. Frozen like base_sha.

concurrency_cap.description: At most this many candidates in flight; clock_in refuses the next.

tokens.description: Tokens one candidate's accounting lines may record.

wallclock_ms.description: duration_ms one candidate's accounting lines may record.

candidate_budget.description: Per candidate, read off its own accounting lines; a candidate that has spent it is refused at clock_in.

question.description: OPTIONAL (#264). The question an investigation answers.

id.description: What a run's `tests` and the conclusion's `supported` name.

claim.description: What the hypothesis says is true.

falsified_by.description: The observation that would refute it, written before any run.

hypotheses.description: OPTIONAL (#264). An investigation declares at least two, or one with `single_hypothesis_rationale`; the batch view, clock_in and clock_out refuse one that does not.

single_hypothesis_rationale.description: OPTIONAL (#264). Why an investigation tests only one hypothesis.

outcome.description: `resolved` needs `supported`, a done run testing it, a done replay of that run, and a done review of either; the other two are never refused.

supported.description: The hypothesis id the evidence supports.

evidence.description: Refs to what was observed: run outputs, commits, files.

conclusion.description: OPTIONAL (#264). Set only through clock_out's `conclusion`, by a unit with `concludes: true`.

agreements.description: OPTIONAL (#261). Working agreements adopted during the job, carried on every brief. Changed only through clock_out's `agreements` {adopt, retire}; each change is recorded in retro[].

budget.description: OPTIONAL (#262). What the job may spend, read back from <checkpoint>.log.jsonl: shiftwork_plan reports spent/remaining/affordable, clock_in refuses a brief that does not fit, and clock_out refuses a 0-token accounting line not marked `estimate`. Absent keeps today's behaviour exactly.

units.description: Accounting lines (clock-outs) the job may record.

wallclock_ms.description: Sum of accounting `duration_ms` the job may record.

cursor.description: THE next unit id. Single pointer — the executor never chooses.

units.description: Flat list, soft cap ~30 units; bigger jobs re-cut via a planner unit.

brief_path.description: Full brief lives in a file, not in the checkpoint.

role.description: Driver dispatch key: role -> model/allowed tools, set in driver config.

attempts.description: This unit's clock-outs, newest last, at most 3 (#259). Written by clock_out from its status and history_entry; clock_in hands them back as prior_attempts and as a dependant's upstream[].last.

reviews.description: Unit ids this unit reviews (#263). Optional. Each must be declared, be in this unit's depends_on, and have a different role from this unit; the batch view, clock_in and clock_out refuse a checkpoint that breaks any of the three.

workspace.description: The worktree the orchestrator created for this candidate, recorded here and removed by the orchestrator after validation.

author_role.description: The role that writes the candidate; must be this unit's role.

candidate.description: OPTIONAL (#265). This unit is a candidate: `touches` does not hold it (its own worktree), its clock-out done reports {kind: commit, ref: <full sha>} and {kind: score, ref: <number>}, and a unit that `reviews` it validates that exact SHA.

tests.description: OPTIONAL (#264). The hypothesis ids this run unit tests; each must be declared. A run clocked out done must report a `produced` item of kind `run-output`.

procedure.description: OPTIONAL (#264). The command or brief path a run follows; a replay must name the same text exactly.

replay_of.description: OPTIONAL (#264). The run this unit repeats: it must be declared, name a procedure equal to this unit's, and be in another role.

concludes.description: OPTIONAL (#264). The unit whose clock_out may set job.conclusion.

irreversible.description: OPTIONAL (#225). The verb of an action that cannot be undone (merge, tag, publish, delete-branch). clock_in refuses such a unit without `prove`, and escalates when job.authorized is declared and does not list the verb.

prove.description: OPTIONAL (#225). A command run against the BUILT artifact (packed tarball, installed wheel), beside `verify`, which checks the source. Required on an `irreversible` unit.

touches.description: Repo-relative POSIX paths this unit will WRITE (#257). Optional; absent or [] claims nothing. The batch view never puts two units sharing a path in one batch, and clock_in refuses a unit whose path a unit still in flight touches.

verify.description: Command proving done-ness. Done-ness is a command, not a claim.

commits.description: Present once a unit has landed work.

repo.description: Staleness guard: must match the working tree at clock-in.

artifacts.description: Files the next session MUST read, with roles.

role.description: Free-form reading role (spec, ledger, ...) — not the unit role enum.

external.description: World-state git cannot see: detached processes, PRs, CI.

until_cmd.description: Wait condition as a shell command; exit 0 = met. The driver waits on this.

history.description: Ring buffer, last 5 units only — the full record is git plus the ledger.

retro.description: What this job taught the loop; patches already applied.

anyOf.description: A decision question: the user's to answer.
#225: a question with a kind. `decision` is the user's; `relay` is answered by its `probe` (shell, exit 0 = answered), which clock_in runs before deciding to escalate.

kind.description: `decision` needs the user; `relay` needs only its probe run.

probe.description: Shell command run from the repo root; exit 0 answers a relay question. Required on a relay: clock_out refuses one without it.

open_questions.description: The autonomy switch: empty = driver keeps cycling, non-empty = STOP and ask — unless every entry is a relay question its probe answers (#225).

do_not.description: Negative space — near-mistakes past sessions made.

notes.description: OPTIONAL. Free-form prose the next session should read that no other key names: a gate baseline, the last commit, a technique worth reusing. A STRING, not a map: every key sessions tried to carry here before this field existed was an attempt to say one sentence, and a map keyed by fact would grow a key per session — the journal the ≤ 2 KB index posture bans, one level down, and an object no schema can close. The same word means the same thing as `history[].notes`. Empty is legal: `handoff` is shallow-merged at clock-out, so a note outlives the unit that wrote it until a later session overwrites it, and the empty string is that overwrite. Declaring this key is what keeps `handoff` closed — a sentence has a home, so an unknown sibling is still a typo and still refused.
